lead_en: Every living thing, from a blade of grass to a hawk in the sky, has to find energy, grow, and leave young behind. See how a leaf makes food from sunlight, how a caterpillar becomes a butterfly, and why a mudflat is one of the busiest places on the coast.
lead_zh: 每一種生物，從一根小草到天上的老鷹，都得取得能量、長大、留下後代。看一片葉子怎麼用陽光做出食物、毛毛蟲怎麼變成蝴蝶，還有為什麼一片泥灘是海岸上最熱鬧的地方。

intro.en: Every lesson starts with something you can find near your school: a leaf, a sparrow, a line of ants. A 3D model shows what is going on inside, one idea at a time, and an English reading explains it, with Chinese a tap away.
intro.zh: 每一課都從學校附近找得到的東西開始：一片葉子、一隻麻雀、一排螞蟻。先用 3D 模型看清楚裡面發生了什麼事，一課只講一個道理；再讀一篇英文短文把它說明白，中文翻譯隨點隨看。

intro.en: The lessons are grouped into four units: cells and life, plants, animals, and living together. When a lesson touches something already explained in The Human Body, How Things Work, or Earth and Weather, it links there instead of explaining it twice.
intro.zh: 課程分成四個單元：細胞與生命、植物、動物、生態。遇到「人體探索」「萬物原理」或「地球與天氣」已經講過的東西，就直接連過去，不重講一次。

intro.en: Every number is checked against a source listed at the bottom of each lesson. Each lesson also tells you clearly which parts of its model are real and which are only a picture.
intro.zh: 每一個數字都查證過，出處列在每課最下方。每一課也會清楚告訴你，模型裡哪些是真的、哪些只是示意。

units.blurb_en: What every living thing is built of, where food begins, and the instructions inside every cell.
units.blurb_zh: 所有生物是用什麼蓋成的、食物最初從哪裡來，還有每個細胞裡的那份說明書。

lessons.title: What Is a Cell?
lessons.blurb_en: A whale, a mushroom, a blade of grass, and you are all built from the same kind of tiny living block. It is called a cell. In a 3D model, cut one open and tap each part to see what it does. Then switch to a plant cell and find the three things it has that yours do not. Last, learn to tell what kind of cell you are looking at.
lessons.blurb_zh: 鯨魚、香菇、一根小草，還有你，都是用同一種很小很小的、活的積木蓋成的。它叫做細胞。在 3D 模型裡把一個細胞切開，點一點每個部分，看它在做什麼。接著換成植物細胞，找出它有、你的細胞卻沒有的三樣東西。最後，學會分辨眼前看到的是哪一種細胞。
lessons.big_idea_en: Every living thing is made of cells. A cell is a tiny bag of jelly with a thin skin around it. Inside, a control center holds the instructions, and small power stations turn food into energy. Plant cells have three extra things: a stiff wall, green parts that make food from sunlight, and a big bag of water. Some living things are a single cell. You are about thirty trillion of them, working together.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 所有的生物都是細胞組成的。細胞是一個很小的袋子，外面包著一層薄薄的皮，裡面裝著膠狀的東西。裡面有一個指揮中心保管著說明書，還有一些小小的發電廠把食物變成能量。植物的細胞多了三樣東西：一道硬硬的牆、用陽光做食物的綠色小東西，還有一大袋水。有些生物只有一個細胞；你則是大約三十兆個細胞一起合作的結果。

lab.how_en: Drag to turn the model, and scroll or pinch to zoom. The cell has been cut open so you can see inside. Tap a part in the list. It lights up in the model, and you can read what it does. When you have tried them all, choose Plant cell. Which parts are new? Which part takes up most of the room?
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉模型，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。這個細胞被切開了，讓你看得到裡面。在清單裡點一個部分，它會在模型裡亮起來，並說明它在做什麼。全部試過之後，選「植物細胞」：多了哪些部分？哪一個部分占掉最多的空間？

wall.en: The cell wall is a stiff box around a plant cell. It is built mostly of a tough material called cellulose. It gives the cell its shape and holds the plant up. A tree can stand tall with no bones because it has billions of these little boxes.
wall.zh: 細胞壁是包在植物細胞外面的一個硬盒子，主要是用一種很堅韌的材料「纖維素」做成的。它讓細胞有固定的形狀，也把植物撐起來。樹沒有骨頭卻站得那麼高，就是因為它有幾十億個這樣的小盒子。

membrane.en: The cell membrane is the thin skin of the cell. It keeps the inside in and the outside out, but it is not a wall. It lets some things through and stops others, so the cell can take in what it needs and send out its waste.
membrane.zh: 細胞膜是細胞那層薄薄的皮。它把裡面的東西留在裡面、把外面的擋在外面，不過它並不是一道牆：有些東西它放行，有些它擋住，所以細胞可以把需要的東西收進來，把廢物送出去。

nucleus.en: The nucleus is the control center. It holds almost all of the cell's instructions, written in a long molecule called DNA. The instructions tell the cell what to make and when. Lesson 3 looks inside it.
nucleus.zh: 細胞核是指揮中心。細胞的說明書幾乎都保管在這裡，是寫在一種很長的分子「DNA」上面的。這份說明書告訴細胞要做什麼、什麼時候做。第三課會打開它來看。

mito.en: Mitochondria are the power stations. They take in food and oxygen and turn them into a kind of energy that the rest of the cell can use. A cell that works hard, such as a muscle cell, has a great many of them.
mito.zh: 粒線體是發電廠。它們把食物和氧氣變成細胞其他部分可以使用的能量。工作量大的細胞，例如肌肉細胞，裡面的粒線體特別多。

chloroplast.en: Chloroplasts are the green parts where a plant makes its food. They catch sunlight and use it to turn carbon dioxide and water into sugar. Animal cells have none, which is why you have to eat. Lesson 2 shows them at work.
chloroplast.zh: 葉綠體是植物做食物的地方，也是它綠色的來源。它們抓住陽光，用它把二氧化碳和水變成糖。動物的細胞沒有葉綠體，所以你必須吃東西。第二課可以看到它們怎麼工作。

vacuole.en: The vacuole is a large bag of water in the middle of a plant cell. When it is full, it presses outward against the wall and makes the cell firm. When a plant has too little water, the bags shrink, the cells go soft, and the plant droops.
vacuole.zh: 液泡是植物細胞中間的一大袋水。它裝滿的時候，會往外頂住細胞壁，讓細胞硬挺。植物缺水的時候，這些袋子縮小，細胞變軟，整株植物就垂下來了。

cytoplasm.en: The cytoplasm is the jelly that fills the cell. Everything else floats in it. It is mostly water, and a great deal of the cell's work goes on there.
cytoplasm.zh: 細胞質是填滿細胞的那團膠狀物，其他的東西都浮在裡面。它大部分是水，細胞有很多工作就是在這裡進行的。

legend.en: Green: cell wall (box) and chloroplasts (ovals), in plants only
legend.zh: 綠色：細胞壁（盒子）和葉綠體（橢圓），只有植物有

legend.en: Blue: the large vacuole, in plants only
legend.zh: 藍色：大液泡，只有植物有

lab.scale_en: A teaching model. Real cells are not these colors. Most of a cell is almost clear, and scientists add dyes to see the parts. Real cells also come in many shapes, and they hold other parts that this model leaves out to keep it simple. The parts are not drawn to scale: mitochondria and chloroplasts are drawn larger than they should be so that you can see them.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的模型。真的細胞不是這些顏色：細胞大部分幾乎是透明的，科學家要加染料才看得出各個部分。真的細胞有各式各樣的形狀，裡面還有別的構造，這個模型為了簡單沒有畫出來。各部分也沒有照比例：粒線體和葉綠體畫得比實際大，這樣你才看得到。
lab.credit_html: Model drawn by My Culture Connect as a teaching diagram. The ideas follow the sources listed at the bottom of this page. · 模型由人師教育協會自繪示意；原理依本頁最下方列出的出處。

paras: Look closely at the back of your hand. It seems smooth and solid. But if you could look much, much closer, you would find that your skin is built of tiny separate pieces, packed together like bricks in a wall. Each piece is alive. Each one is called a cell.

Cells were first seen in 1665. An English scientist named Robert Hooke looked at a thin slice of cork through a microscope and saw rows of little empty boxes. They reminded him of the small rooms that monks lived in, which were called cells, so that is the name he gave them. About 170 years later, scientists came to understand that every plant and every animal is made of cells.

A cell is like a very small bag. Its skin is called the cell membrane, and it decides what may come in and what may go out. The bag is filled with a watery jelly. Floating in the jelly is the nucleus, which keeps the cell's instructions. There are also many tiny power stations, called mitochondria, which turn food into energy that the cell can use.

Plant cells have all of these, and three things more. Around the membrane there is a stiff wall, which gives the plant its strength. Inside there are green chloroplasts, which make food from sunlight. And in the middle there is a large bag of water, called a vacuole, which keeps the cell firm.

Some living things are just one cell, alone. A drop of pond water is full of them. Larger living things are made of a great many cells. An adult human body has about thirty trillion. They are not all alike. Nerve cells, muscle cells, skin cells, and blood cells each have a different shape because each has a different job.

Where do new cells come from? Always from other cells. A cell grows, copies its instructions, and divides into two. That is how you grew from a single cell into the person you are, and it is how your skin mends itself after a cut. Every cell alive today came from a cell that lived before it.
paras_zh: 仔細看看你的手背。它看起來又平滑又完整。可是如果你能湊得非常非常近去看，就會發現皮膚是由一小塊一小塊分開的東西排在一起組成的，像牆上的磚頭一樣。每一小塊都是活的。每一塊都叫做細胞。
人類第一次看見細胞是在 1665 年。英國科學家虎克用顯微鏡觀察一片薄薄的軟木，看到一排排小小的空格子。這讓他想到修道士住的小房間，那種房間就叫 cell，所以他用這個字來稱呼它們。大約 170 年以後，科學家才明白：每一種植物、每一種動物，都是細胞組成的。
細胞就像一個非常小的袋子。它的皮叫做細胞膜，由它決定什麼可以進來、什麼可以出去。袋子裡裝滿了含水的膠狀物。浮在膠狀物裡的有細胞核，它保管著細胞的說明書；還有許多小小的發電廠，叫做粒線體，把食物變成細胞可以使用的能量。
這些植物細胞全都有，另外還多三樣。細胞膜外面有一道硬硬的牆，讓植物有力氣站著。裡面有綠色的葉綠體，用陽光做出食物。中間還有一大袋水，叫做液泡，讓細胞保持硬挺。
有些生物就只是一個細胞，獨自生活；一滴池塘的水裡就有很多。比較大的生物是很多很多細胞組成的。一個成年人的身體大約有三十兆個細胞。它們並不是都長得一樣：神經細胞、肌肉細胞、皮膚細胞和血球，形狀各不相同，因為各有各的工作。
新的細胞是從哪裡來的？永遠是從別的細胞來的。一個細胞長大、把說明書複製一份，然後分裂成兩個。你就是這樣從一個細胞長成現在的你；割傷之後皮膚會自己長好，也是這個道理。今天活著的每一個細胞，都來自在它之前活著的細胞。

sorter.en: What kind of cell is this?
sorter.lead_en: Imagine that you are looking down a microscope. Tick what you can see, and find out what kind of cell it probably is.
sorter.lead_zh: 想像你正在看顯微鏡。把你看到的打勾，看看它大概是哪一種細胞。

animal.note_en: No wall, no chloroplasts, and no large vacuole. It could be a cell from your cheek, from a fish, or from a fly.
animal.note_zh: 沒有細胞壁、沒有葉綠體，也沒有大液泡。它可能是你臉頰內側的細胞，也可能來自一條魚或一隻蒼蠅。

green.note_en: It has all three. This is a cell from a part of a plant that lives in the light, such as a leaf.
green.note_zh: 三樣都有。這是植物照得到光的部分的細胞，例如葉子。

root.en: A plant cell that lives in the dark
root.note_en: It has a wall and a vacuole but no chloroplasts. Cells in a root are like this. They cannot make food, so the leaves send sugar down to them.
root.note_zh: 有細胞壁和液泡，卻沒有葉綠體。根裡面的細胞就是這樣。它們沒辦法自己做食物，要靠葉子把糖送下來。

odd.note_en: Plants and animals do not usually have cells like this. Look again. In a plant cell the wall, the chloroplasts, and the vacuole usually come together.
odd.note_zh: 植物和動物通常沒有這樣的細胞。再看一次吧：在植物細胞裡，細胞壁、葉綠體和液泡通常是一起出現的。

items.en: Robert Hooke saw the little boxes in a slice of cork and named them cells.

items.en: Matthias Schleiden and Theodor Schwann put forward the idea that all plants and animals are made of cells.

items.en: Each human cell holds roughly two meters of DNA, folded up inside a nucleus far too small to see.
items.zh: 人的每一個細胞裡大約有兩公尺長的 DNA，摺疊在小到看不見的細胞核裡。

items.en: Plant cells have three things that animal cells lack: a wall, chloroplasts, and a large vacuole.
items.zh: 植物細胞比動物細胞多三樣東西：細胞壁、葉綠體和大液泡。

items.en: Many living things are a single cell, and every one of us began as a single cell.

culture_cards.title_zh: 一片軟木、小小的動物、一條規則，還有兩種奇特的細胞
culture_cards.lead_en: How people found cells, and a few that break the pattern.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 人們是怎麼發現細胞的，還有幾種不照常理來的細胞。

cards.body_en: Robert Hooke built his own microscope and looked at everything he could find: a flea, a snowflake, the point of a needle. In a thin slice of cork he saw rows of tiny boxes and called them cells. What he saw were not living cells. Cork is dead bark, and the boxes were the empty walls that the cells had left behind.
cards.body_zh: 虎克自己做了顯微鏡，拿它觀察所有找得到的東西：跳蚤、雪花、針尖。在一片薄薄的軟木裡，他看到一排排小格子，把它們叫做 cell。其實他看到的並不是活的細胞：軟木是死掉的樹皮，那些格子是細胞留下來的空牆。

cards.body_en: At about the same time, a cloth seller in the Netherlands named Antonie van Leeuwenhoek was grinding tiny lenses of his own. Through them he saw things that nobody had seen before: living creatures swimming in a drop of water. He called them little animals. He was the first person to see living things made of a single cell.
cards.body_zh: 差不多同一個時候，荷蘭有一位布商雷文霍克，自己磨出了很小的鏡片。透過這些鏡片，他看到了從來沒有人看過的東西：在一滴水裡游來游去的小生物。他把牠們叫做「小動物」。他是第一個看見單細胞生物的人。

cards.body_en: By the middle of the 1800s, scientists had agreed on a few simple statements. All living things are made of cells. The cell is the smallest unit of life. And every cell comes from a cell that lived before it. Together these are called cell theory, and nobody has found a living thing that breaks them.
cards.body_zh: 到了十九世紀中葉，科學家對幾句簡單的話有了共識：所有的生物都是細胞組成的；細胞是生命最小的單位；每一個細胞都來自在它之前活著的細胞。這幾句話合起來叫做「細胞學說」，到現在還沒有人找到違反它的生物。

cards.body_en: Your red blood cells break one of the rules in this lesson. When they are fully grown they have no nucleus at all. They throw it out to make more room for carrying oxygen. And although most cells are far too small to see, a human egg cell is one of the largest cells in the body, just big enough to see without a microscope.
cards.body_zh: 你的紅血球打破了這一課裡的一條規則：它們長成熟以後，完全沒有細胞核——把細胞核丟掉，騰出更多空間來載運氧氣。另外，雖然大部分的細胞小到看不見，人的卵細胞卻是身體裡最大的細胞之一，剛好大到不用顯微鏡也看得到。

myths.myth_en: Cells are flat, like the pictures in a book.
myths.myth_zh: 細胞是扁平的，像書上的圖那樣。
myths.fact_en: Cells are solid shapes, like balls, boxes, and long threads. A picture shows only one slice.
myths.fact_zh: 細胞是立體的，像球、盒子或長長的線。圖片畫出來的只是其中一個切面。

myths.myth_en: Only animals are made of cells.
myths.myth_zh: 只有動物是細胞組成的。
myths.fact_en: Plants, mushrooms, and tiny living things in pond water are all made of cells too.
myths.fact_zh: 植物、香菇，還有池塘水裡的微小生物，也都是細胞組成的。

myths.myth_en: All the cells in your body are the same.
myths.myth_zh: 你身體裡的細胞都長得一樣。
myths.fact_en: They come in many shapes for many jobs. A nerve cell is long and thin, and a red blood cell is a small disk.
myths.fact_zh: 它們為了不同的工作，有各式各樣的形狀。神經細胞又細又長，紅血球是小小的圓盤。

myths.myth_en: Plant cells have a wall instead of a membrane.
myths.myth_zh: 植物細胞只有細胞壁，沒有細胞膜。
myths.fact_en: They have both. The membrane lies just inside the wall.
myths.fact_zh: 它們兩樣都有，細胞膜就貼在細胞壁的裡面。

tricks.body_en: The membrane chooses what goes in and out.

tricks.body_zh: 粒線體把食物變成能量。

tricks.body_en: A wall, chloroplasts, and a vacuole.

materials.en: A school microscope, a glass slide, a cover slip, and a dropper of water
materials.zh: 學校的顯微鏡、載玻片、蓋玻片，還有一支裝了水的滴管

materials.en: A piece of onion, and tweezers

steps.en: Break a layer of the onion and peel off the thin, clear skin from its inner side with the tweezers.
steps.zh: 把洋蔥的一層鱗片折斷，用鑷子從內側撕下那層又薄又透明的皮。

steps.en: Lay the skin flat in a drop of water on the slide, and lower the cover slip onto it gently.
steps.zh: 把這層皮平鋪在載玻片上的一滴水裡，再輕輕蓋上蓋玻片。

steps.en: Look through the microscope, starting with the lowest power. Draw what you see.
steps.zh: 從最低倍率開始，用顯微鏡觀察。把你看到的畫下來。

steps.en: Which parts from the model can you find? Which parts are missing, and why might that be?
steps.zh: 模型裡的哪些部分你找得到？哪些找不到？可能是什麼原因？

activities.tip_en: You should see rows of boxes, each with a wall. You will not see any green chloroplasts, because this part of an onion grows in the dark. Ask your teacher before you use any stain, and handle glass slides with care.
activities.tip_zh: 你應該會看到一排排有牆的格子。你找不到綠色的葉綠體，因為洋蔥的這個部分是長在暗處的。要用染劑之前先問老師，拿玻片的時候要小心。

materials.en: A zip-top bag, clear jelly or hair gel, and a small box that the bag just fits into
materials.zh: 一個夾鏈袋、透明的果凍或髮膠，還有一個剛好裝得下袋子的小盒子

materials.en: Small things to be the parts: a grape, a few beans, green peas, and a small balloon filled with water
materials.zh: 當作各個部分的小東西：一顆葡萄、幾顆豆子、青豆，還有一個裝了水的小氣球

steps.en: Fill the bag halfway with the jelly. This is the cytoplasm, and the bag is the membrane.
steps.zh: 把果凍裝到袋子的一半。這是細胞質，袋子就是細胞膜。

steps.en: Add the grape for the nucleus and the beans for the mitochondria. Seal the bag. You have made an animal cell.
steps.zh: 放進葡萄當細胞核、豆子當粒線體，把袋子封好。你做出了一個動物細胞。

steps.en: Now make a second bag. This time add green peas for chloroplasts and the water balloon for the vacuole, and put the bag inside the box.
steps.zh: 再做第二袋。這一次多放青豆當葉綠體、水球當液泡，然後把袋子放進盒子裡。

steps.en: Press gently on each one. Which keeps its shape better? What does the box stand for?
steps.zh: 輕輕壓一壓這兩個細胞。哪一個比較不容易變形？盒子代表的是什麼？

activities.tip_en: The box is the cell wall. Stack several boxes, and you will see how plants can build something tall and strong out of soft, wet cells. Do not eat anything from the model.
activities.tip_zh: 盒子就是細胞壁。把幾個盒子疊起來，你就會明白植物怎麼用又軟又溼的細胞蓋出又高又堅固的東西。模型裡的東西不要吃。

sources.en: Cells were discovered by Robert Hooke in 1665, who named them after the cells of a monastery; cell theory was developed through the work of Schleiden in 1838 and Schwann in 1839; a typical adult human body has about 30 trillion cells; living things can be single-celled or made of many cells of different types
sources.zh: 細胞由虎克於 1665 年發現，並以修道院的小房間命名；細胞學說經許來登（1838）與許旺（1839）的研究建立；成年人體約有 30 兆個細胞；生物可以是單細胞或由許多不同類型的細胞組成

sources.en: Cell theory: all living things are made of cells, the cell is the basic unit of life, and all cells come from cells that already exist
sources.zh: 細胞學說：所有生物都由細胞組成；細胞是生命的基本單位；所有細胞都來自既有的細胞

sources.en: The cell membrane separates the inside of the cell from the outside and lets only some things pass
sources.zh: 細胞膜把細胞內部與外界分開，並且只讓部分物質通過（半透膜）

sources.en: The nucleus contains nearly all of the cell's DNA; each human cell holds roughly two meters of it
sources.zh: 細胞核含有細胞幾乎全部的 DNA；每個人類細胞約有兩公尺長的 DNA

sources.en: Mitochondria produce the chemical energy that the cell uses, and are nicknamed the powerhouse of the cell
sources.zh: 粒線體製造細胞使用的化學能，有「細胞的發電廠」之稱

sources.en: Plant cells have walls containing cellulose, parts that carry out photosynthesis, and a large vacuole that keeps the cell firm
sources.zh: 植物細胞的特徵：含纖維素的細胞壁、能行光合作用的構造、調節膨壓的大液泡

sources.en: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek was the first to observe single-celled living things, with lenses he made himself
sources.zh: 雷文霍克用自己製作的單片鏡顯微鏡，最早觀察到微生物

sources.en: Mature human red blood cells have no nucleus
sources.zh: 人類成熟的紅血球沒有細胞核

sources.en: The human egg cell is one of the largest cells in the body and can be seen without a microscope
sources.zh: 人類的卵細胞是體內最大的細胞之一，不用顯微鏡就看得到

lessons.title: How Does a Leaf Make Food from Sunlight?
lessons.title_zh: 葉子怎麼用陽光做出食物？
lessons.blurb_en: A plant never eats, yet it grows from a tiny seed into a tall tree. Where does all that stuff come from? In a 3D model of a leaf cut open, give it light, air, and water, and watch it make sugar and give off oxygen. Take one of the three away and see what happens. Then find out why almost everything you eat began as sunlight on a leaf.
lessons.blurb_zh: 植物從來不吃東西，卻能從一顆小小的種子長成一棵大樹。那麼多的東西是從哪裡來的？在一片切開的葉子的 3D 模型裡，給它光、空氣和水，看它怎麼做出糖、放出氧氣。再拿掉其中一樣，看看會怎麼樣。最後找出答案：為什麼你吃的東西，幾乎每一樣最初都是照在葉子上的陽光？
lessons.big_idea_en: A leaf is a food factory that runs on sunlight. It takes in carbon dioxide from the air and water from the roots. With the energy of light, it joins them into sugar, and it gives off oxygen. The plant uses the sugar to live and to grow. The leaf needs all three things at once: light, carbon dioxide, and water. Whichever one is shortest sets the speed.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 葉子是一座用陽光發動的食物工廠。它從空氣裡吸進二氧化碳，從根部得到水，再用光的能量把它們結合成糖，同時放出氧氣。植物靠這些糖活著、長大。葉子同時需要三樣東西：光、二氧化碳和水；最缺的那一樣，決定它做得多快。

lab.how_en: Drag to turn the model, and scroll or pinch to zoom. This is a slice of a leaf, seen from the side and made much larger. Follow the five kinds of dots: yellow light, gray carbon dioxide, blue water, orange sugar, and pale green oxygen. Then move the three sliders one at a time. What happens to the sugar when you turn the light down? What happens to the little holes underneath when you take the water away?
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉模型，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。這是一片葉子的切面，從側面看，而且放大了很多倍。跟著五種小點走：黃色是光、灰色是二氧化碳、藍色是水、橘色是糖、淺綠色是氧氣。接著一次只動一支滑桿：把光調暗，糖怎麼了？把水拿掉，底下那些小孔又怎麼了？

go.en: The leaf has plenty of light, carbon dioxide, and water, so the factory is running fast. Sugar flows out along the vein to the rest of the plant, and oxygen drifts out through the small holes underneath.
go.zh: 光、二氧化碳和水都很充足，工廠全速運轉。糖沿著葉脈送到植物的其他部位，氧氣從底下的小孔飄出去。

light.en: There is plenty of carbon dioxide and water, but not enough light. Light is the energy that joins them together, so the leaf can only work as fast as the light allows. Adding more water or air will not help.
light.zh: 二氧化碳和水都夠，可是光不夠。光是把它們結合起來的能量，所以光有多少，葉子就只能做多快。這時候再多給水或空氣也沒有用。

co2.en: There is plenty of light and water, but the leaf is short of carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide is where the carbon in sugar comes from. Without enough of it, the light has little to work on.
co2.zh: 光和水都夠，可是二氧化碳不夠。糖裡面的碳就是從二氧化碳來的；二氧化碳不夠，光再強也沒有東西可以加工。

water.en: The leaf is short of water. Look at the small holes underneath: they are closing. That saves water, but it also shuts out the carbon dioxide. A thirsty plant in bright sun cannot make much food.
water.zh: 葉子缺水了。看看底下的小孔：它們正在關起來。這樣可以省水，可是二氧化碳也被擋在外面了。大太陽下口渴的植物，做不出多少食物。

dark.en: It is dark, and the factory has stopped. No sugar is being made, and no oxygen is given off. The small holes have closed for the night. The plant now lives on the sugar it made during the day.
dark.zh: 天黑了，工廠停工了。沒有糖做出來，也沒有氧氣放出來，底下的小孔也關起來過夜。這時候植物靠白天做好的糖過日子。

legend.en: Gray dots: carbon dioxide coming in
legend.zh: 灰色的點：進來的二氧化碳

legend.en: Blue dots: water coming in along the vein
legend.zh: 藍色的點：沿著葉脈進來的水

legend.en: Orange cubes: sugar going out along the vein
legend.zh: 橘色小方塊：沿著葉脈送出去的糖

legend.en: Pale green dots: oxygen going out
legend.zh: 淺綠色的點：出去的氧氣

legend.en: Dark green balls: chloroplasts, where the sugar is made
legend.zh: 深綠色小球：葉綠體，做糖的地方

lab.scale_en: A teaching model. A real leaf is only a fraction of a millimeter thick, and this slice is drawn very much larger and far tidier than a real one. The percentages on the sliders are not measurements; they only mean a little or a lot. The rule that the shortest supply sets the speed is a simple picture of something more complicated. The counts of sugar and oxygen follow the real recipe: six oxygen for every sugar. Light is not really made of dots that pile up in a leaf.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的模型。真的葉子只有零點幾公釐厚，這個切面畫得大了非常多倍，也比真的整齊得多。滑桿上的百分比不是測量值，只代表「少」或「多」。「最缺的那一樣決定速度」是把比較複雜的事情簡化之後的說法。糖和氧氣的數目照的是真的配方：每做一顆糖，放出六個氧氣。光其實也不是一顆一顆堆在葉子裡的小點。
lab.credit_html: Model drawn by My Culture Connect as a teaching diagram. The ideas follow the sources listed at the bottom of this page. · 模型由人師教育協會自繪示意；原理依本頁最下方列出的出處。

paras: You have to eat to stay alive. So does a dog, a bird, and a fish. But a tree stands in one place for a hundred years and never eats a thing. All the same, it grows. A seed that weighs less than a coin becomes a trunk too heavy to lift. Where does all that wood come from?

For a long time people thought the answer was the soil. About four hundred years ago, a scientist named Jan van Helmont tested the idea. He planted a small willow tree in a pot of soil and gave it nothing but water for five years. The tree gained about 74 kilograms. The soil had lost only 57 grams. So the tree was not made of soil.

The real answer is in the leaves. A leaf takes in a gas called carbon dioxide from the air, through tiny holes on its underside. Water comes up from the roots. Inside the leaf there are small green parts called chloroplasts. They catch the energy of sunlight and use it to join the carbon dioxide and the water into sugar.

This is called photosynthesis, which means putting together with light. Sugar is the plant's food. It burns some for energy, and it builds the rest into leaves, roots, and wood. So most of a tree is made from air and water, joined together by sunlight.

Something is left over when sugar is made: oxygen. The leaf lets it out through the same tiny holes, and it mixes into the air. That oxygen comes from the water, not from the carbon dioxide. It is the gas that you, and nearly every other animal, must breathe to stay alive.

Now think about your last meal. Rice, bread, and vegetables are parts of plants. Meat and eggs come from animals that ate plants. Follow any food back far enough, and you arrive at a green leaf in the sun. In a way, you run on sunlight too.
paras_zh: 你必須吃東西才能活下去，狗、鳥和魚也一樣。可是一棵樹在同一個地方站了一百年，從來沒有吃過任何東西，卻照樣長大。一顆比硬幣還輕的種子，可以長成重到搬不動的樹幹。那麼多的木頭是從哪裡來的？
很長一段時間，人們以為答案是土壤。大約四百年前，一位叫做范．海爾蒙特的科學家做了實驗來檢驗這個想法。他把一棵小柳樹種在一盆土裡，五年當中只給它澆水。這棵樹增加了大約 74 公斤，土卻只少了 57 公克。所以樹並不是土做的。
真正的答案在葉子裡。葉子透過背面細小的孔，從空氣中吸進一種叫做二氧化碳的氣體；水則從根部送上來。葉子裡面有一些綠色的小東西，叫做葉綠體。它們抓住陽光的能量，用它把二氧化碳和水結合成糖。
這件事叫做「光合作用」，意思是「用光來合成」。糖就是植物的食物：一部分燒掉當作能量，其餘的拿來長出葉子、根和木頭。所以一棵樹的大部分，是空氣和水做的，是陽光把它們接在一起的。
做糖的時候會多出一樣東西：氧氣。葉子從同樣那些小孔把它放出去，混進空氣裡。這些氧氣是從水來的，不是從二氧化碳來的。它就是你和幾乎所有動物都必須呼吸才能活下去的那種氣體。
現在想一想你上一餐吃了什麼。米飯、麵包和青菜是植物的一部分；肉和蛋來自吃植物的動物。任何一種食物，只要往回追得夠遠，都會追到一片曬著太陽的綠葉。從某個角度來說，你也是靠陽光在運轉的。
questions: What did van Helmont's willow tree show?
What three things does a leaf need to make sugar?
Where does the oxygen that a leaf gives off come from?
answers: The tree gained about 74 kilograms while the soil lost only 57 grams, so a tree is not made of soil.
It needs light, carbon dioxide from the air, and water from the roots.
It comes from the water. It is left over when the leaf joins water and carbon dioxide into sugar.

parts.text_en: The holes are wide open, and sugar pours out along the vein.
parts.text_zh: 氣孔大開，糖沿著葉脈不斷送出去。

parts.text_en: Air and water are waiting, but there is not enough energy to join them.
parts.text_zh: 空氣和水都在等，可是沒有足夠的能量把它們接起來。

parts.text_en: The holes close to save water, and the carbon dioxide is shut out.
parts.text_zh: 氣孔關起來省水，二氧化碳也被擋在外面。

parts.text_en: The factory stops. The counters stand still until morning.
parts.text_zh: 工廠停工，數字不再增加，要等到天亮。

lessons.parts_note_en: On the cloudy day, try adding more water or more carbon dioxide. Does the sugar go up? Only the thing in shortest supply can speed the leaf up.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 在陰暗的日子裡，試著多加一點水或二氧化碳：糖有變多嗎？只有補上最缺的那一樣，葉子才快得起來。

recipe.lead_en: Photosynthesis follows an exact recipe. Choose how many sugars the leaf should make, and count what it needs and what is left over.
recipe.lead_zh: 光合作用有一份精確的配方。選一選葉子要做幾顆糖，再數一數它需要什麼、又多出了什麼。
recipe.rule_en: The recipe never changes: 6 carbon dioxide and 6 water make 1 sugar and 6 oxygen. Nothing is lost. Every atom that goes in comes out again in the sugar or in the oxygen.
recipe.rule_zh: 這份配方永遠不變：6 個二氧化碳加 6 個水，做出 1 顆糖和 6 個氧氣。什麼都沒有少：放進去的每一個原子，都在糖或氧氣裡面。
recipe.note_en: The sugar here is glucose. Each dot stands for one molecule, the smallest bit of a substance. A real leaf makes an enormous number of them every second, and it needs light for every one.
recipe.note_zh: 這裡的糖是葡萄糖。每一個點代表一個分子，也就是一種物質最小的一份。真的葉子每一秒都做出數量龐大的分子，而且每一個都需要光。

items.en: A leaf needs light, carbon dioxide, and water, all at the same time.

items.en: Six carbon dioxide and six water make one sugar and six oxygen.
items.zh: 6 個二氧化碳加 6 個水，做出 1 顆糖和 6 個氧氣。

items.en: Van Helmont's willow gained about this much in five years, while its soil lost only 57 grams.

culture_cards.title_en: The willow, the bubbles, the color green, and the rice in your bowl
culture_cards.title_zh: 一棵柳樹、一串氣泡、綠色，還有你碗裡的飯
culture_cards.lead_en: How people worked it out, and where you can see it today.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 人們是怎麼弄懂的，還有今天在哪裡看得到。

cards.body_en: Jan van Helmont weighed a pot of soil, planted a small willow in it, and watered it for five years. Then he weighed everything again. The tree had gained about 74 kilograms, and the soil had lost only 57 grams. He decided that the tree was made of water. He was half right. He did not know that the air was giving it something too.
cards.body_zh: 范．海爾蒙特先秤了一盆土的重量，在裡面種下一棵小柳樹，澆了五年的水，然後把所有東西重新秤一次。樹大約增加了 74 公斤，土只少了 57 公克。他的結論是：樹是水做的。他對了一半。他不知道，空氣也給了這棵樹東西。

cards.body_en: Jan Ingenhousz put green plants under water and watched. In sunlight, small bubbles rose from the green parts. In the shade, the bubbles stopped. The plants were making a gas, and they needed light to do it. That was the missing piece. In the 1900s, another scientist, Cornelis van Niel, showed that the oxygen in those bubbles comes from water that the plant has split apart.
cards.body_zh: 英根豪斯把綠色的植物放在水裡觀察。在陽光下，綠色的部分冒出一顆顆小氣泡；到了陰影裡，氣泡就停了。植物正在製造一種氣體，而且需要光才做得到。這就是缺少的那一塊拼圖。到了二十世紀，另一位科學家范尼爾證明，氣泡裡的氧氣來自被植物拆開的水。

cards.body_en: Sunlight is a mix of many colors. The green stuff in a leaf, called chlorophyll, takes in mostly the blue light and the red light and uses their energy. It takes in much less of the green, so the green light bounces off and reaches your eyes. The color you see is the part of the sunlight that the leaf uses least.
cards.body_zh: 陽光是很多種顏色混在一起的。葉子裡綠色的東西叫做葉綠素，它主要吸收藍光和紅光，利用它們的能量；綠光吸收得少得多，所以被反射出來、進到你的眼睛。你看到的顏色，其實是陽光裡葉子用得最少的那一部分。

cards.body_en: Changhua County grows so much rice that it has been called the rice barn of Taiwan. Stand beside a paddy field on a sunny day, and you are looking at this lesson at work. Every leaf is taking in air and water and making sugar. The plant packs that sugar into its seeds as starch, and those seeds are the grains of rice in your bowl.
cards.body_zh: 彰化縣盛產稻米，有「臺灣米倉」的稱號。大晴天站在稻田旁邊，你看到的就是這一課正在發生的事：每一片葉子都在吸進空氣和水、做出糖。稻子再把這些糖變成澱粉，存進種子裡；那些種子，就是你碗裡的一粒粒米飯。

myths.myth_en: Plants get their food from the soil.
myths.myth_zh: 植物的食物是從土裡來的。
myths.fact_en: Plants make their own food from air and water, using light. From the soil they take water and small amounts of minerals.
myths.fact_zh: 植物用光，把空氣和水做成自己的食物。它們從土裡吸收的是水和少量的礦物質。

myths.myth_en: A tree is made mostly of soil.
myths.myth_zh: 一棵樹大部分是土做的。
myths.fact_en: Most of a tree is made from carbon dioxide and water. Van Helmont's soil lost only 57 grams while his tree gained 74 kilograms.
myths.fact_zh: 樹的大部分是二氧化碳和水做的。范．海爾蒙特的土只少了 57 公克，樹卻增加了 74 公斤。

myths.myth_en: The oxygen that leaves give off comes from carbon dioxide.
myths.myth_zh: 葉子放出來的氧氣是從二氧化碳來的。
myths.fact_en: It comes from water. The plant splits water apart, keeps what it needs, and lets the oxygen go.
myths.fact_zh: 它是從水來的。植物把水拆開，留下需要的部分，把氧氣放掉。

myths.myth_en: Leaves are green because they use green light.
myths.myth_zh: 葉子是綠的，因為它們用的是綠光。
myths.fact_en: It is the opposite. Leaves use mostly blue and red light. Green is the color they use least, so it is the color that bounces back.
myths.fact_zh: 正好相反。葉子主要用的是藍光和紅光；綠光用得最少，所以被反射回來。

tricks.body_en: From the roots, along the veins.
Sugar is made in the green parts.

materials.en: A clear glass or bowl of water and a fresh green leaf (a water plant works best)
materials.zh: 一個裝了水的透明杯子或碗，還有一片新鮮的綠葉（水草效果最好）

materials.en: A sunny windowsill, a dark cupboard, and a clock
materials.zh: 一個曬得到太陽的窗台、一個黑暗的櫃子，還有時鐘

steps.en: Put the leaf under the water. Use a small stone to hold it down if it floats.
steps.zh: 把葉子放進水裡。如果它浮起來，用一顆小石頭壓住。

steps.en: Stand the glass in bright sunlight for one hour. Look closely at the leaf. What do you see on it?
steps.zh: 把杯子放在明亮的陽光下一個小時。仔細看葉子：上面出現了什麼？

steps.en: Tap the glass gently and wipe the bubbles off. Now put it in the dark cupboard for one hour.
steps.zh: 輕輕敲一敲杯子，把氣泡抹掉。然後把它放進黑暗的櫃子裡一個小時。

steps.en: Look again. Are there as many bubbles as before? What made the difference?
steps.zh: 再看一次。氣泡和剛才一樣多嗎？差別是什麼造成的？

activities.tip_en: This is the experiment Ingenhousz did in 1779. The bubbles in sunlight are mostly oxygen. Some bubbles may also form just because the water warms up, so compare the sunny glass with the dark one before you decide.
activities.tip_zh: 這就是英根豪斯在 1779 年做的實驗。陽光下的氣泡大部分是氧氣。不過水變暖本身也會冒出一些氣泡，所以要拿曬太陽的那一杯和放在暗處的那一杯比過，再下結論。

materials.en: A healthy potted plant with large leaves
materials.zh: 一盆葉子比較大的健康盆栽

materials.en: Black paper or aluminum foil, and paper clips
materials.zh: 黑紙或鋁箔紙，還有迴紋針

steps.en: Choose one leaf and leave it on the plant. Cover part of it, on both sides, with a strip of black paper, and hold the paper in place with paper clips.
steps.zh: 選一片葉子，不要摘下來。用一條黑紙把它的一部分上下兩面都遮住，用迴紋針固定。

steps.en: Leave the plant in a sunny place for one week. Water it as usual.
steps.zh: 把盆栽放在曬得到太陽的地方一個星期，照平常那樣澆水。

steps.en: Take the paper off. Compare the part that was covered with the rest of the leaf.
steps.zh: 把黑紙拿掉。比一比被遮住的部分和葉子的其他部分。

steps.en: What color is the covered part? What do you think happened to it?
steps.zh: 被遮住的地方是什麼顏色？你覺得它發生了什麼事？

activities.tip_en: The covered part could not make any food, and the plant stopped keeping it green. Take the clips off gently, and the leaf will usually recover in the light. Use a plant that belongs to you or to your class.
activities.tip_zh: 被遮住的部分沒辦法做出食物，植物也不再讓它保持綠色。輕輕把迴紋針拿掉，葉子曬到光之後通常會慢慢恢復。請用自己或班上的盆栽來做。

sources.en: Photosynthesis turns light energy into chemical energy, splitting water to release oxygen and fixing carbon dioxide into sugar; discovered in 1779 by Jan Ingenhousz, who showed that plants need light; plants usually convert 3 to 6% of light; about 100 to 115 billion tons of carbon become biomass each year
sources.zh: 光合作用把光能轉成化學能，分解水放出氧氣，並把二氧化碳固定成糖；1779 年由英根豪斯發現，他證明植物需要光；植物通常把 3–6% 的光轉成化學能；每年約 1,000–1,150 億噸的碳變成生物量

sources.en: Van Helmont's five-year willow experiment: the tree gained about 74 kg while the soil lost only 57 grams, and he concluded that the gain came from water
sources.zh: 范．海爾蒙特的五年柳樹實驗：樹增加約 74 公斤，土只少了 57 公克；他推論增加的重量來自水

sources.en: In sunlight, plants under water give off bubbles from their green parts, and in the shade the bubbles stop
sources.zh: 在陽光下，水中植物的綠色部分會冒出氣泡，在陰影中氣泡就停止

sources.en: Plants give off oxygen by splitting water, not carbon dioxide
sources.zh: 植物放出的氧氣來自分解水，而不是二氧化碳

sources.en: A stoma is a pore in the skin of a leaf, bordered by two guard cells that control how wide it opens; gases pass through it, and water vapor leaves through it
sources.zh: 氣孔是葉子表皮上的小孔，由兩個保衛細胞控制開合；氣體經由它進出，水氣也從這裡散失

sources.en: Chlorophyll absorbs mainly blue and red light, and green light is absorbed less, which is why plants look green
sources.zh: 葉綠素主要吸收藍光和紅光，綠光吸收得比較少，所以植物看起來是綠色的

sources.en: In most leaves the main food-making tissue is a layer of tall cells on the upper side
sources.zh: 大部分的葉子，主要進行光合作用的組織是靠近上表面的柵狀組織

sources.en: Changhua County is known for its rice and has been called the rice barn of Taiwan
sources.zh: 彰化縣盛產稻米，有「臺灣米倉」之譽
sources.src: 維基百科「彰化縣」（引《田中鎮志》）

lessons.title: What Is DNA?
lessons.blurb_en: Inside almost every one of your cells there is a set of instructions for building you. It is written with only four letters. In a 3D model, unzip a piece of DNA and watch each half build itself a new partner, until one molecule has become two that match. Then change a single letter and see where the change goes. Last, write a code of your own and count how many different codes four letters can make.
lessons.blurb_zh: 你身上幾乎每一個細胞裡，都有一套把你做出來的說明書。它只用四個字母寫成。在 3D 模型裡把一段 DNA 解開，看兩邊各自補上新的搭檔，一個分子變成一模一樣的兩個。接著換掉一個字母，看看這個改變會跑到哪裡去。最後自己寫一段密碼，算一算四個字母能排出多少種不同的密碼。
lessons.big_idea_en: DNA is a very long molecule shaped like a twisted ladder. Each rung of the ladder is a pair of chemical letters, and there are only four letters: A, T, C, and G. A always pairs with T, and C always pairs with G. The order of the letters is the message. Because of the pairing rule, a cell can pull the ladder apart and rebuild both halves, so every new cell gets its own full copy.
lessons.big_idea_zh: DNA 是一種非常長的分子，形狀像一條扭起來的梯子。梯子的每一根橫槓是一對化學字母，而字母總共只有四個：A、T、C、G。A 一定配 T，C 一定配 G。字母排列的順序，就是訊息的內容。因為有這條配對規則，細胞可以把梯子從中間拉開，再把兩半各自補齊，所以每一個新的細胞都拿得到完整的一份。

lab.how_en: Drag to turn the model, and scroll or pinch to zoom. Press Pause, and then move the slider slowly from 0 to 100. The ladder opens from the top like a zipper, and new letters join each half. Look at which letter joins which. Then tap any letter in the row under the slider to change it, and copy the ladder again. Do both copies carry your change?
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉模型，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。先按「暫停」，再把滑桿從 0 慢慢拉到 100。梯子會像拉鍊一樣從上面打開，新的字母接到兩邊。注意看哪個字母接上哪個字母。接著在滑桿下面那一排字母裡點任何一個，把它換掉，再複製一次。兩份都帶著你改的那個字母嗎？

closed.en: This is a short piece of DNA with twelve rungs. Each rung is a pair of letters. Look closely: A is always joined to T, and C is always joined to G. Move the slider to unzip it.
closed.zh: 這是一小段 DNA，有十二根橫槓。每一根橫槓是一對字母。仔細看：A 永遠和 T 接在一起，C 永遠和 G 接在一起。拉動滑桿把它解開。

opening.en: The two strands are coming apart. Each loose letter can take only one partner, so each old strand works as a pattern for a new one. The new strands are drawn in orange.
opening.zh: 兩股正在分開。每一個落單的字母都只能接受一種搭檔，所以每一股舊的都成了新的一股的樣板。新的那一股用橘色畫出來。

done.en: Now there are two ladders, and they read exactly the same. Each one has one old strand and one new strand. This is how a cell copies its instructions before it divides.
done.zh: 現在有兩條梯子了，而且讀起來一模一樣。每一條都是一股舊的加一股新的。細胞在分裂之前，就是這樣把說明書複製一份。

changed.en: You changed a letter, and its partner changed with it, because the pairing rule still holds. A change in the letters of DNA is called a mutation. Now unzip the ladder and see what happens to your change.
changed.zh: 你換了一個字母，它的搭檔也跟著換了，因為配對規則還是一樣。DNA 的字母發生改變，叫做突變。現在把梯子解開，看看這個改變會怎麼樣。

donechanged.en: Both copies carry your change. The copying follows the letters that are there. It does not know what they used to be. This is why a change in DNA is passed on to every cell that comes from this one.
donechanged.zh: 兩份都帶著你改的地方。複製的時候只照著眼前的字母，並不知道它原本是什麼。所以 DNA 一旦改變，就會傳給這個細胞之後分裂出來的每一個細胞。

legend.en: Red: the letter T, the partner of A
legend.zh: 紅色：字母 T，A 的搭檔

legend.en: Yellow: the letter G, the partner of C
legend.zh: 黃色：字母 G，C 的搭檔

legend.en: Pale beads: the two old strands
legend.zh: 淺色的珠子：原來的兩股

legend.en: Orange beads: the two new strands
legend.zh: 橘色的珠子：新接上的兩股

lab.scale_en: A teaching model. The twelve letters are an example and are not taken from a real gene. Real DNA has no colors, and its letters are groups of atoms, not printed letters. The ladder turns once in about ten rungs, as real DNA does, but the two sides are drawn evenly spaced to keep the picture simple. In a cell, copying is done by many helper molecules that the model does not show, and one set of human DNA has about 3.1 billion rungs, not twelve.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的模型。這十二個字母是舉例，並不是取自哪一個真的基因。真的 DNA 沒有顏色，它的「字母」是一小群原子，不是印出來的字。梯子大約每十根橫槓轉一圈，這一點和真的 DNA 一樣；不過為了畫面簡單，兩邊畫成等距。在細胞裡，複製是靠許多幫忙的分子完成的，模型沒有畫出來；而人的一套 DNA 大約有三十一億根橫槓，不是十二根。
lab.credit_html: Model drawn by My Culture Connect as a teaching diagram. The ideas follow the sources listed at the bottom of this page. · 模型由人師教育協會自繪示意；原理依本頁最下方列出的出處。

paras: Identical twins can look so much alike that even their friends mix them up. Why? Both of them grew from the same single cell, so both carry almost exactly the same set of instructions. Those instructions are written in a molecule called DNA.

DNA is very long and very thin, and it is shaped like a ladder that has been twisted. Scientists call this shape a double helix. The two sides of the ladder are long strands. The rungs between them are made of four small chemical parts, which we call by their first letters: A, T, C, and G.

The letters follow one simple rule. A always pairs with T, and C always pairs with G. So each rung is a pair, and if you know the letters along one side of the ladder, you can work out the letters along the other side.

This rule is what lets a cell copy its DNA. Before a cell divides, the ladder unzips down the middle. Each loose letter picks up a new partner, A with T and C with G, until there are two ladders where there was one. They read the same, and each has one old strand and one new strand.

The order of the letters is the message. A stretch of DNA that carries the instructions for one job is called a gene. People have about 19,000 to 20,000 genes that tell cells how to build proteins. One full set of human DNA has about 3.1 billion pairs of letters, and it is packed into 23 pairs of bundles called chromosomes.

Now and then a letter is changed. This is called a mutation. Many mutations make no difference at all, and some change how a living thing is built. Every living thing we know, from a mushroom to an orchid to you, writes its instructions with the same four letters. Only the order is different.
paras_zh: 同卵雙胞胎可以長得非常像，連朋友都會認錯。為什麼？因為他們兩個是從同一個細胞長出來的，所以身上帶著幾乎一模一樣的一套說明書。這套說明書寫在一種叫做 DNA 的分子裡。
DNA 非常長，也非常細，形狀像一條被扭轉過的梯子。科學家把這種形狀叫做雙螺旋。梯子的兩邊是兩股長長的鏈子，中間的橫槓由四種小小的化學零件組成，我們用它們英文名字的第一個字母來稱呼：A、T、C、G。
這些字母遵守一條簡單的規則：A 一定和 T 配對，C 一定和 G 配對。所以每一根橫槓都是一對；只要知道梯子其中一邊的字母，就能推出另一邊的字母。
細胞能複製 DNA，靠的就是這條規則。細胞分裂之前，梯子會從中間像拉鍊一樣解開。每一個落單的字母都接上一個新的搭檔，A 配 T、C 配 G，直到原來的一條梯子變成兩條。這兩條讀起來一樣，而且每一條都是一股舊的加一股新的。
字母的順序就是訊息。DNA 上面負責一件工作的那一段說明，叫做基因。人類大約有一萬九千到兩萬個基因，告訴細胞怎麼製造蛋白質。人的一整套 DNA 大約有三十一億對字母，收在二十三對叫做染色體的小捆裡。
偶爾會有一個字母被換掉，這叫做突變。很多突變一點影響也沒有，有些則會改變生物長出來的樣子。我們知道的每一種生物，從香菇、蘭花到你，都用同樣的四個字母寫說明書，不一樣的只有順序。
questions: What is the pairing rule for the four letters?
How does a cell copy its DNA?
answers: It is shaped like a twisted ladder. Scientists call this shape a double helix.
A always pairs with T, and C always pairs with G.
The ladder unzips down the middle, and each loose letter picks up a new partner, until there are two ladders that read the same.

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: Twelve rungs, each one a pair. Check every rung against the rule.
parts.text_zh: 十二根橫槓，每一根都是一對。把每一根都拿規則對一對。

parts.text_en: The top is open and the bottom is still closed. Find the place where new letters are joining.
parts.text_zh: 上面打開了，下面還合著。找出新的字母正在接上去的地方。

parts.text_en: Read the two ladders from top to bottom. Each has one pale strand and one orange strand.
parts.text_zh: 把兩條梯子從上往下讀一遍。每一條都有一股淺色的、一股橘色的。

parts.text_en: One letter is changed, and then the ladder is copied. Look for the change in both copies.
parts.text_zh: 換掉一個字母，然後把梯子複製一次。在兩份裡找找那個改變。

lessons.parts_note_en: Try to break the rule. However you change the letters, an A never ends up joined to a C. The shapes of the real letters only fit together in these two ways.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 試試看能不能打破規則。不管你怎麼換字母，A 都不會和 C 接在一起。真正的那些「字母」，形狀就只有這兩種接法合得起來。

links.note_zh: 回去找一找細胞核——細胞保管 DNA 的地方。

coder.eyebrow: Write in DNA · 用 DNA 寫字
coder.en: How much can four letters say?
coder.lead_en: Press the letters to write one strand. Its partner strand appears underneath, and the number shows how many different codes of that length there could be.
coder.lead_zh: 按字母寫出其中一股，它的搭檔會出現在下面；右邊的數字告訴你，這個長度一共可以寫出多少種不同的密碼。
coder.note_en: Each place can hold any of the four letters, so every letter you add makes four times as many possible codes.
coder.note_zh: 每一個位置都可以放四個字母裡的任何一個，所以每多加一個字母，可能的密碼就變成四倍。
coder.out_en: A cell reads its DNA three letters at a time, and three letters can be arranged in 64 ways. One set of human DNA is about 3.1 billion pairs of letters long.
coder.out_zh: 細胞一次讀三個字母，而三個字母有 64 種排法。人的一套 DNA 大約有三十一億對字母那麼長。

facts.eyebrow: DNA by the Numbers · DNA 的數字
facts.zh: 六個和 DNA 有關的數字
facts.lead_en: From four letters to three billion.

items.en: A, T, C, and G. Every living thing we know uses the same four.
items.zh: A、T、C、G。我們知道的每一種生物，用的都是這四個。

items.en: Friedrich Miescher first separated DNA from cells. He did not yet know what it was for.
items.zh: 米歇爾第一次把 DNA 從細胞裡分離出來。當時他還不知道它有什麼用。

items.en: James Watson and Francis Crick published the double helix shape of DNA.
items.zh: 華生和克里克發表了 DNA 的雙螺旋結構。

items.en: About this many pairs of letters make up one set of human DNA.
items.zh: 人的一套 DNA，大約由這麼多對字母組成。

items.en: Human cells carry their DNA in 23 pairs of chromosomes, 46 in all.
items.zh: 人的細胞把 DNA 收在 23 對染色體裡，一共 46 條。

items.en: Cells read DNA three letters at a time. Four letters taken three at a time give 64 combinations.
items.zh: 細胞一次讀三個字母。四個字母每次取三個，有 64 種組合。

culture_cards.title_en: Bandages, a photograph, a very long book, and an orchid
culture_cards.title_zh: 繃帶、一張照片、一本很長的書，還有一種蘭花
culture_cards.lead_en: How people found DNA, saw its shape, and learned to read it.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 人們怎麼找到 DNA、看出它的形狀，又怎麼學會讀它。

cards.zh: 在用過的繃帶上發現的
cards.body_en: A young Swiss doctor named Friedrich Miescher wanted to know what cells are made of. He collected used bandages from a hospital, because the pus on them was full of cells. In the nuclei of those cells he found a substance that nobody had described before. He called it nuclein. Today we call it DNA.
cards.body_zh: 年輕的瑞士醫生米歇爾想知道細胞是什麼東西做的。他從醫院收集用過的繃帶，因為上面的膿含有大量的細胞。在這些細胞的細胞核裡，他找到一種從來沒有人描述過的物質，把它叫做「核素」。今天我們叫它 DNA。

cards.body_en: On May 2, 1952, at King's College London, Raymond Gosling took an X-ray picture of DNA while working under Rosalind Franklin. It is known as Photo 51, and it became an important piece of evidence for the shape of DNA. On April 25, 1953, James Watson and Francis Crick published the double helix in the journal Nature. Watson, Crick, and Maurice Wilkins shared a Nobel Prize in 1962. Franklin had died in 1958.
cards.body_zh: 1952 年 5 月 2 日，在倫敦國王學院，葛斯林在富蘭克林的指導下拍下一張 DNA 的 X 光照片，後來被稱為「第 51 號照片」，成為判斷 DNA 形狀的重要證據。1953 年 4 月 25 日，華生和克里克在《自然》期刊發表了雙螺旋結構。1962 年，華生、克里克和威爾金斯共同獲得諾貝爾獎；富蘭克林已經在 1958 年過世。

cards.body_en: In 1990, scientists in many countries began the Human Genome Project. Their aim was to read every letter of human DNA. The project was declared complete on April 14, 2003, with about 92 percent of the letters read. The parts that were hardest to read took much longer. A complete sequence with no gaps was reported in 2022.
cards.body_zh: 1990 年，許多國家的科學家展開「人類基因體計畫」，目標是把人類 DNA 的每一個字母都讀出來。這個計畫在 2003 年 4 月 14 日宣布完成，當時讀出了大約 92% 的字母。最難讀的那些部分又花了很久，直到 2022 年，才有沒有缺口的完整序列發表。

cards.body_en: Phalaenopsis equestris is a small moth orchid that is native to Taiwan and the Philippines, and growers often use it as a parent when they breed new orchids. In 2014, a team of scientists that included researchers at National Cheng Kung University in Tainan published its genome in the journal Nature Genetics. They counted 29,431 predicted genes for building proteins.
cards.body_zh: 桃紅蝴蝶蘭（又叫姬蝴蝶蘭）是一種小型的蝴蝶蘭，原生於台灣和菲律賓，也是育種者培育新品種時常用的親本。2014 年，一個包含台南國立成功大學研究人員在內的科學團隊，在《自然—遺傳學》期刊發表了它的基因體。他們預測出 29,431 個製造蛋白質的基因。

myths.myth_en: DNA is found only in blood.
myths.fact_en: It is in the cells of every part of you, such as your skin, your hair roots, and the inside of your cheek.
myths.fact_zh: 你身體每個部位的細胞裡都有，例如皮膚、髮根，還有臉頰內側。

myths.myth_en: Only people and animals have DNA.
myths.myth_zh: 只有人和動物才有 DNA。
myths.fact_en: Plants, mushrooms, and bacteria have it too, written with the same four letters.
myths.fact_zh: 植物、香菇和細菌也都有，而且用的是同樣的四個字母。

myths.myth_en: A change in DNA is always harmful.
myths.myth_zh: DNA 只要改變就一定有害。
myths.fact_en: Many changes make no difference. Some do harm, and a few turn out to be useful.
myths.fact_zh: 很多改變完全沒有影響；有些有害，也有少數後來反而有用。

myths.myth_en: Identical twins are the same in every way.
myths.myth_zh: 同卵雙胞胎每一個地方都一樣。
myths.fact_en: Their DNA is nearly identical, but they are two different people. Even their fingerprints are not the same.
myths.fact_zh: 他們的 DNA 幾乎一樣，卻是兩個不同的人，連指紋都不相同。

tricks.body_en: Two strands with rungs between them.
A, T, C, and G, in a long row.
A pairs with T, and C pairs with G.
tricks.body_zh: A 配 T，C 配 G。

materials.en: Paper in four colors, scissors, and a pen
materials.zh: 四種顏色的紙、剪刀和一支筆

materials.en: A long table or a clear space on the floor
materials.zh: 一張長桌，或地上的一塊空位

steps.en: Cut about twenty small cards of each color. Write A on one color, T on the next, and then C and G.
steps.zh: 每種顏色各剪大約二十張小卡。在一種顏色上寫 A，另一種寫 T，其餘兩種寫 C 和 G。

steps.en: Lay ten cards in a column, in any order you like. Beside each one, place its partner. You have made a ladder.
steps.zh: 隨意排十張卡，排成一直行。在每一張旁邊放上它的搭檔。你做出了一條梯子。

steps.en: Slide the two columns apart. Now give every card a new partner from the cards that are left.
steps.zh: 把兩行往兩邊拉開。接著用剩下的卡片，替每一張卡找一個新的搭檔。

steps.en: Read the two ladders from top to bottom. Are they the same? Which cards in each ladder are the old ones?
steps.zh: 把兩條梯子從上往下讀一遍。它們一樣嗎？每一條梯子裡，哪些卡是原來的？

activities.tip_en: Ask a friend to swap one card while you look away, before you slide the columns apart. After copying, can you find the change in both ladders?
activities.tip_zh: 在把兩行拉開之前，請朋友趁你沒看的時候偷偷換掉一張卡。複製完以後，你能在兩條梯子裡都找到那個改變嗎？

materials.en: A partner to send a message to
materials.zh: 一位可以互傳訊息的夥伴

steps.en: Make a code table together. Give each letter of the alphabet its own three-letter word made only of A, T, C, and G, such as AAA for a and AAT for b.
steps.zh: 兩個人一起做一張密碼表。替每一個英文字母指定一組只用 A、T、C、G 排成的三字組合，例如 AAA 代表 a、AAT 代表 b。

steps.en: Write a short word in your code, as one long row of letters with no spaces.
steps.zh: 用你們的密碼寫一個短短的英文字，寫成一長串、中間不留空格。

steps.en: Trade messages, and read your partner's message three letters at a time.
steps.zh: 互相交換訊息，然後一次讀三個字母，把對方的訊息解出來。

steps.en: Now change one letter in the row, and read it again. What happens to the word?
steps.zh: 現在把那一串裡的一個字母換掉，再讀一次。那個字變成什麼了？

activities.tip_en: There are 64 three-letter words and only 26 letters in the alphabet, so you have plenty to spare. Cells have spare ones too. Their 64 words stand for only about 20 building blocks, so several words can mean the same thing.
activities.tip_zh: 三字組合一共有 64 種，英文字母只有 26 個，所以綽綽有餘。細胞也一樣有多的：它的 64 種組合只代表大約 20 種積木，所以好幾種組合可以是同一個意思。

sources.en: DNA is made of two strands that coil around each other in a double helix; it carries the genetic instructions of all known living things; its four bases are cytosine (C), guanine (G), adenine (A), and thymine (T); Friedrich Miescher first isolated it in 1869, from pus on discarded surgical bandages, and called it nuclein
sources.zh: DNA 由兩股互相纏繞成雙螺旋的鏈組成，攜帶所有已知生物的遺傳指令；四種鹼基為 C、G、A、T；米歇爾 1869 年從廢棄手術繃帶上的膿首次分離出 DNA，稱為核素（nuclein）

sources.en: A pairs with T through two hydrogen bonds, and G pairs with C through three
sources.zh: A 與 T 以兩個氫鍵配對，G 與 C 以三個氫鍵配對

sources.en: In DNA replication each original strand serves as a template for a new partner strand, so each new molecule has one old strand and one new strand
sources.zh: DNA 複製時，原來的每一股各自作為模板合成互補的新股，所以每個新分子都是一股舊的加一股新的（半保留複製）

sources.en: The most common form of DNA is a right-handed double helix with about 10 to 10.5 base pairs in each turn
sources.zh: 最常見的 B 型 DNA 是右旋的雙螺旋，每轉一圈約 10 到 10.5 個鹼基對

sources.en: The human reference genome contains approximately 3.1 billion base pairs and between 19,000 and 20,000 protein-coding genes; a complete sequence of a human genome was reported in 2022
sources.zh: 人類參考基因體約有 31 億個鹼基對、約 19,000 到 20,000 個蛋白質編碼基因；2022 年發表完整的人類基因體序列

sources.en: Human cells have 23 pairs of chromosomes, 46 in all
sources.zh: 人類細胞有 23 對、共 46 條染色體

sources.en: The genetic code is read three letters at a time and can be written as a table with 64 entries, which stand for the 20 standard amino acids
sources.zh: 遺傳密碼一次讀三個核苷酸，可以寫成一張 64 格的表，對應 20 種標準胺基酸

sources.en: Photo 51 was taken by Raymond Gosling, working under Rosalind Franklin at King's College London, on May 2, 1952
sources.zh: 第 51 號照片由葛斯林在富蘭克林指導下，於 1952 年 5 月 2 日在倫敦國王學院拍攝

sources.en: Watson and Crick published the double helix structure in Nature on April 25, 1953
sources.zh: 華生與克里克的雙螺旋論文刊於 1953 年 4 月 25 日的《自然》
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Molecular Structure of Nucleic Acids: A Structure for Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid”

sources.en: Crick, Watson, and Wilkins shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1962; Rosalind Franklin died on April 16, 1958
sources.zh: 克里克、華生、威爾金斯於 1962 年共同獲得諾貝爾生理學或醫學獎；富蘭克林於 1958 年 4 月 16 日過世

sources.en: The Human Genome Project officially launched in 1990 and was declared complete on April 14, 2003, when it included about 92% of the genome
sources.zh: 人類基因體計畫 1990 年正式啟動，2003 年 4 月 14 日宣布完成，當時涵蓋約 92% 的基因體

sources.en: Identical twins develop from one fertilized egg and are genetically nearly identical; they do not have the same fingerprints
sources.zh: 同卵雙胞胎由同一個受精卵發育而來，基因幾乎相同；兩人的指紋並不相同

sources.en: Mutations in genes can have no effect, can alter what the gene makes, or can stop the gene from working properly
sources.zh: 基因的突變可能沒有影響，可能改變基因的產物，也可能使基因無法正常運作

sources.en: The genome of the orchid Phalaenopsis equestris, a frequently used parent species for orchid breeding, contains 29,431 predicted protein-coding genes; the authors include researchers at National Cheng Kung University (published online November 24, 2014)
sources.zh: 桃紅蝴蝶蘭（姬蝴蝶蘭；育種常用的親本）的基因體含 29,431 個預測的蛋白質編碼基因；作者群包含國立成功大學的研究人員（2014 年 11 月 24 日線上發表）
sources.src: Cai et al., “The genome sequence of the orchid Phalaenopsis equestris,” Nature Genetics

sources.en: Phalaenopsis equestris is native to the Philippines and Taiwan
sources.zh: 桃紅蝴蝶蘭（姬蝴蝶蘭）原生於菲律賓與台灣
